porous inert materials can reduce noise from combustion in a swirling combustor.
porous inert rings located within the reaction zone are effective at reducing combustion noise in a swirled combustor.
porous inert media can be used to manipulate combustion and reduce noise in gas turbine combustors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of passive techniques for the reduction of combustion noise from gas turbines and other combustion systems.
the development of passive techniques for noise mitigation using porous inert media.
developing a new technology for noise mitigation in gas turbine engines using passive manipulation of the combustion process by using high strength, oxidation-resistant PIMs.

the PIM ring configuration and geometry can be optimized for a specific combustor design, and that the use of PIM rings is an attractive approach to mitigate combustion noise.
the PIMS are effective in reducing combustion noise in the combustor.

the use of PIM in the combustion chamber is a promising passive noise mitigation technique.
the PIM geometry has a significant impact on the combustion noise.
the porous inert material (PIM) rings can be used as a passive control method in reducing noise levels in gas turbines.
